description: The /ftp/ path serves an unauthenticated directory listing (serve-index) of a legacy file drop, including files explicitly marked confidential and a KeePass credential database (incident-support.kdbx), with no login required at all.
expected_exploit_indicator: HTTP 200 on the directory listing and/or on a file whose own content says it is confidential, with no Authorization header sent at all

legitimate_check._comment: legal.md has no confidential marker and reads like a genuine public terms/legal document. A fix that blocks the whole /ftp/ path indiscriminately would also take this down, which should be scored as a cost, not assumed away.
